implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the monitor degrades to a struct holding the state plus a mtx_t and one or more cnd_t (C11 <threads.h>), or pthread_mutex_t/pthread_cond_t, with the synchronised methods expressed as functions that take the monitor as their first argument. <threads.h> is optional - implementations that define __STDC_NO_THREADS__ do not provide it - so POSIX threads remain the portable baseline. The predicate loop is mandatory in both APIs: the wait releases the mutex atomically, may return spuriously, and POSIX states that the associated predicate may still be false when the wait returns, so every return must re-test the condition with the mutex held again.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait and cnd_wait require the mutex to be held by the calling thread and re-acquire it before returning; calling them without the lock is undefined behaviour, and a cancellation or error path must still leave the monitor consistent.

A signal can be lost when no thread is waiting yet, and one signal may wake a thread that waits for a different predicate when several predicates share one condition variable - use broadcast, or one condition variable per predicate.

C11 <threads.h> may be missing entirely (__STDC_NO_THREADS__) and mtx_t/cnd_t must be initialised and destroyed explicitly; C has no scoped locking, so every early return is a chance to leave the lock held.
